notes: JPEG bytes with a .txt extension. `UTType(filenameExtension: "txt")` conforms to neither .image nor .movie, so the scanner never sees this file.
The metadata reader would happily read it — this entry pins the reader, not the scanner.
PNG bytes with a .jpg extension: ImageIO sniffs content, so the read succeeds anyway. Only the SCANNER cares about the extension.
PNG with no metadata: everything nil/empty.
XMP in a PNG iTXt chunk is read exactly like XMP in a JPEG APP1.
Header-only JPEG: ImageIO opens the source but there are no usable properties.
A zero-byte file yields no CGImageSource properties — but the sidecar is still read, so tags survive.
The sidecar read is unconditional; it does not depend on the image opening.
Falls through to DateTimeDigitized when DateTimeOriginal is absent.
Date order is DateTimeOriginal → DateTimeDigitized → TIFF DateTime.
SubSecTimeOriginal (250) and OffsetTimeOriginal (+02:00) are DROPPED: the format string is exactly "yyyy:MM:dd HH:mm:ss" and neither field is consulted. Subsecond is always .000.
Orientation is not read by the app at all — the core parses it for its own decode path and the app never asks for it.
LANDMINE: hour 24 is ACCEPTED and rolls into the next day — 2021:07:04 24:00:00 becomes 2021-07-05T00:00:00.
So the parser is strict about out-of-range months/days but lenient about hour 24. A naive strict `%H` (0..=23) parse in Rust would return nil instead.
Month 13 / day 45 is rejected by the non-lenient parser, so DateTimeDigitized wins.
No EXIF, no XMP, no sidecar: every field nil/empty.
Falls through to TIFF:DateTime (exiftool ModifyDate) when both EXIF dates are absent.
The "0000:00:00 00:00:00" camera sentinel is REJECTED by the non-lenient formatter (month 00 is out of range), so the walk falls through to DateTimeDigitized.
A chrono parser that accepts month 0 / day 0 would diverge here.
Both coordinates are required; a lone latitude yields nil/nil.
Missing refs mean no negation — the values stay positive (northern/eastern).
GPSAltitude / GPSAltitudeRef are read by nobody — the reader has no altitude field.
Ref "S"/"W" negate the (always positive) magnitudes.
GPSAltitudeRef=1 (below sea level) is ignored along with the altitude.

SUB-ULP DIVERGENCE, pinned to the port's value: the longitude reads -151.20929999999998 where ImageIO's Swift reader gave -151.2093 — one ULP apart, 1e-14 degrees, a nanometre on the ground. The two differ only in the order they fold degrees/minutes/seconds out of the EXIF rationals. The Rust host test compares GPS at 1e-9 and is indifferent; this file is byte-exact, so the number here is the port's.

LANDMINE, CONFIRMED: the ref comparison is case-SENSITIVE (`latRef == "S"` / `lonRef == "W"`). The raw lowercase refs "s"/"w" written here do NOT negate, so this southern/western point is reported as northern/eastern.
exiftool normalises refs to uppercase on a normal write; these were planted with `#=` to bypass PrintConv, which is why the case matters at all.

Latitude 0 comes out as +0. When the ref IS uppercase the same expression yields -0.0, which serialises as `-0` in JSON — see gps/south_west.jpg's sign handling and keep Rust's float formatting in mind.
SUB-ULP DIVERGENCE, same cause as gps/south_west.jpg: the longitude reads 9.999999999999999e-05 where ImageIO gave 0.0001. One ULP.
Uppercase extension. The scanner lowercases before UTType lookup; the sidecar manifest keys on the lowercased basename.
Multiple dots. The sidecar is `dotted.name.v2.jpg.xmp` (full basename + .xmp), NOT `dotted.name.v2.xmp`.
`filename` in PhotoFile drops only the LAST extension, so it becomes "dotted.name.v2".
Non-BMP characters in the filename (single scalar, so NFC/NFD is not a factor here — see stable_uuid_vectors.json for that).
Spaces and parentheses in the name; sidecar lookup is `url.appendingPathExtension("xmp")`, i.e. it operates on path components, not on a re-parsed string.
digiKam order (Name then Area) — the look-behind finds the correct name for every region.
Coordinates as child elements: the parser concatenates the open tag with everything up to `</mwg-rs:Area>` before running the field lookup.
KNOWN BUG, PINNED AS-IS: exiftool serialises struct fields alphabetically, so Area precedes Name.
`parseMWGRegions` locates each `<mwg-rs:Area>` and then searches BACKWARDS for the nearest mwg-rs:Name, which in this ordering is the PREVIOUS region's name.
Result is an off-by-one: region 0 gets no name at all, region i gets region i-1's name, and the last name is lost.
The Rust port must reproduce this. Fixing it is a separate, deliberate change with its own LibrarySnapshot version bump.
KNOWN BUG, PINNED AS-IS: an unterminated `<mwg-rs:Area` followed by a well-formed one finds the LATER `</mwg-rs:Area>`.
The attribute blob then spans both regions, the coordinates come from the malformed (first) Area, and the second region is swallowed — one region out, not two.
An unterminated `<mwg-rs:Area` with nothing after it is skipped; earlier regions survive.
Attribute form `mwg-rs:Name="…"` is tried before element form `<mwg-rs:Name>`.
The name look-behind window is 2000 characters. A name further back than that is not found and the region ends up unnamed.
A coordinate that fails Double() drops that region only.
stArea:unit="pixel" is rejected; a missing unit is accepted; the comparison is `unit?.lowercased() == "normalized"`, so "Normalized" is accepted too.
Rejected regions are skipped silently, they do not abort the walk.
A region with no mwg-rs:Name anywhere in the look-behind window is emitted with name = nil.
Both "photo-tools:CountryCode" and "phototools:CountryCode" are probed, in that order.
The precedence table, all in one file:
tags = UNION, embedded first; the case-insensitive dedup is first-wins, so the EMBEDDED spelling of a conflicting path survives ("People/Alice", not the sidecar's "people/alice").
countryCode = EMBEDDED wins (IT, not FR).
faceRegions = SIDECAR wins outright when non-empty — the embedded region is discarded, not merged.
Sidecar fills the country only when the embedded packet has none.
LANDMINE: the sidecar parser reads exactly three things — digiKam:TagsList, photo-tools:CountryCode, MWG regions.
exif:DateTimeOriginal and exif:GPS* in a sidecar are ignored entirely; dateTaken and GPS stay nil.
Dedup key is `raw.lowercased()`, first occurrence wins — "people/alice" and "PEOPLE/ALICE" collapse into the first "People/Alice".
"People/Alice/Child" is a different path and survives.
Empty and whitespace-only rdf:li entries are dropped; surviving values are whitespace-trimmed.
A non-XML sidecar parses to nothing; there is no error surface, the photo just looks untagged.
The "mwg-rs present but no Areas parsed" branch logs a warning and returns an empty region list.
A sidecar with no regions leaves the embedded regions in place (the swap is guarded on non-empty).
The surviving embedded region is unnamed — see xmp/regions_digikam_order.jpg for why.
No embedded metadata: the sidecar supplies tags, country and regions.
rdf:Bag works exactly like rdf:Seq: the parser only scans for `<rdf:li>` between the TagsList open and close tags.
The open-tag probe is `<digiKam:TagsList>` first, then `<digiKam:TagsList ` (with the trailing space) for attribute-carrying forms.
No `</digiKam:TagsList>` means the whole block is skipped — a truncated sidecar silently yields zero tags rather than a partial list.
UTF-16 (BOM-prefixed) sidecars decode through the String(data:encoding:.utf16) fallback.
LANDMINE: an ISO-branded MP4 carrying the same `moov/udta/©day` reads as nil. AVFoundation only honours udta/©day for QuickTime-branded files.
A Rust atom parser that reads udta/©day unconditionally would be MORE permissive than the Swift baseline — that is a behaviour change, not a bug fix.
A QuickTime-branded container with an .mp4 extension still resolves — AVFoundation dispatches on content, the scanner on extension.
LANDMINE: a zone-less ©day is read as UTC by AVFoundation, NOT as device-local — unlike EXIF dates, which are device-local.
So the two date paths in this app disagree about what a zone-less timestamp means.
No udta at all: AVAsset.creationDate is nil and the pipeline falls back to filesystem dates (see EarliestFilesystemDateTests).
QuickTime `moov/udta/©day` with an explicit +0000 offset.
CountryCode is uppercased on read ("it" → "IT").
LANDMINE: CountryCode is matched by LEAF NAME only, so IPTC's Iptc4xmpCore:CountryCode competes with photo-tools:CountryCode.
First tag enumerated wins (`countryCode == nil` guard). The order comes from ImageIO's XMP walk, not from the packet's byte order.
Tags + country + regions + EXIF date in one file, no sidecar.
The single embedded region comes back with name = nil for the reason above, even though the packet names it "Alice".
Embedded regions are recovered by re-serialising the packet with CGImageMetadataCreateXMPData and running the same string parser as the sidecar path.
LANDMINE, CONFIRMED: ImageIO re-serialises struct fields ALPHABETICALLY, so Area always lands before Name — no matter how the packet was written.

That means EVERY embedded MWG region in this app hits the backwards-Name off-by-one described on regions/exiftool_order.jpg. This file was written in digiKam order (Name first) and still comes back mis-named.
Consequence for the port: embedded regions are currently shifted by one and the first is unnamed. The sidecar path is the only one that gets names right.
Same regions as regions_digikam_order but written Area-before-Name. The output is IDENTICAL — proof that the input packet's element order is erased by ImageIO's re-serialisation.
LANDMINE: only digiKam:TagsList is read. lr:hierarchicalSubject and dc:subject are invisible to the app even when they disagree.
The tag match is on the LEAF NAME "TagsList", so any namespace declaring a TagsList would also be picked up.
Embedded digiKam:TagsList is read through CGImageMetadataCopyTags; rdf:Seq members arrive as nested CGImageMetadataTags, not strings.
